news-version-d37ba793e.text:
`commit:abd7e49d`: user-visible, not in NEWS. I could only see the first 2000 diff lines, which are mostly CI files, so I judged this commit from its diffstat and tests. Most of its behaviour changes are in the NEWS top section: separation warnings, jackknife with fewer than 5 units, the RMST fixed horizon, the KK strat-Cox fixes, the studentized g-comp bootstrap, the censored-data bootstrap guards, covariate-dropped warnings and the reusable-worker fixes. One user-visible fix has no entry. The test `test-bootstrap-subset-warm-start-policy-and-binomial-infeasible-start.R` (v1.0.6-TODO-142) shows two changes: bootstrap subset copies made outside an active resampling operation now follow the non_param_boot warm-start policy, and the identity/log binomial kernels now pull an infeasible OLS cold start into the mean support. Before, those fits returned converged = FALSE and the R class silently dropped covariates.
Draft for `Bug fixes`:
* `InferenceIncidLogBinomial` and `InferenceIncidBinomialIdentityRiskDiff` cold fits no longer start outside the mean support: the OLS smart cold start often put mu outside [0, 1] (identity) or eta > 0 (log), so the constrained kernel returned `converged = FALSE` after one iteration and the class silently dropped covariates. The start is now pulled into the support. Bootstrap subset copies made outside an active resampling operation (for example in `ci_calibrated_bootstrap()`'s outer loop) also now follow the `non_param_boot` warm-start policy instead of keeping the parent's warm start, so the same draw no longer fits differently by call path (v1.0.6-TODO-142).

news-version-d85b2b0ca.text:
`commit:ff5486d7`: user-visible, not in NEWS. `InferencePropBetaRegr` fits could be handed a warm-start coefficient vector of the wrong length. This happens on a resampled draw where QR drops a column. The kernel rejected the start and the fit returned NULL. The QR loop then dropped a real covariate, so a leave-one-block-out jackknife draw fitted x only instead of x + s, and the worker estimate was off by about 1e-3. The fix discards a mis-sized warm start. NEWS covers rank-deficient resamples for about 30 classes (v1.0.6-TODO-123), but it doesn't describe this warm-start length bug in the beta class.
Draft for `Bug fixes`:
* `InferencePropBetaRegr`: a bootstrap or jackknife draw that drops a rank-deficient column no longer reuses a warm-start coefficient vector from the full-data fit, which has one more column. The kernel rejected it, the fit returned `NULL`, and the hardened refit then dropped a real covariate (a leave-one-block-out jackknife draw fitted `x` instead of `x + s`, shifting the worker estimate by about 1e-3). A start of the wrong length is now ignored and the fit starts cold.

news-version-dc5e82fc5.text:
`commit:c28bbb34`: user-visible, not in NEWS. The non-concave randomization warm-start change is in the top NEWS section. Two other user-visible changes are not. The tie-tolerance rewrite (`rand_tie_tolerance`, scaled by max(|t|, |draws|), also applied to studentized randomization-bootstrap p-values and the closed-form CI) and the `InferenceIncidExactZhang` CI fix were written into the `# EDI 1.0.4` section of NEWS.md, which is already tagged. Both are post-v1.0.4 behaviour changes, so they belong in the development section. The tie-tolerance entry is also marked Breaking in the 1.0.4 section; the Zhang one sits under that section's Bug fixes.
Draft for `Changes that alter results`:
* Randomization p-values (and their Monte Carlo bands, the studentized randomization-bootstrap p-values and the closed-form randomization-bootstrap CI) now count a redrawn statistic as a tie in both tails when it is within `sqrt(.Machine$double.eps)` times max(|observed|, largest |redraw|) of the observed one, instead of 1e-8 times |observed|. This covers an observed statistic of exactly 0 (an enumerated 12-subject `InferenceOrdinalRidit` test gave p = 0.9935 instead of 1). P-values with such ties can only rise. `InferenceIncidExactZhang$compute_exact_confidence_interval()` (and the `type = "Zhang"` randomization CI for incidence) now inverts the combined test it reports, starting its endpoint search from a point that test accepts; intervals that already started from an accepted point do not change.

news-version-df7342378.text:
`commit:e00ab78f`: user-visible, not in NEWS. The robust-regression kernel and `maxit` changes are in the top NEWS section (the "C++ robust-regression kernel" bullet). The `DesignFixedRerandomization` change is not: the constructor now stops when neither `obj_val_cutoff` nor `prop_acceptable` is given, and `SimulationFramework` supplies `prop_acceptable = 0.1` when no rule is given. The commit put it in the tagged `# EDI 1.0.4` section, not the development section, so the top section does not describe it.
Draft for `Breaking changes`:
* `DesignFixedRerandomization$new()` now requires an acceptance rule, exactly one of `obj_val_cutoff` and `prop_acceptable`, and stops if neither is given. Before, giving neither accepted every candidate draw, so the design was complete randomization with a fixed number treated. Pass e.g. `prop_acceptable = 0.1` (keep the best 10% of draws by Mahalanobis distance); `obj_val_cutoff = Inf` reproduces the old behaviour exactly. `SimulationFramework` supplies `prop_acceptable = 0.1` when the design is given without a rule.
